newsitem.title: USA: US Stockpile sells aluminum, talk of Brown absence.
newsitem.headline: US Stockpile sells aluminum, talk of Brown absence.

text.p: U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center said it sold 10,210 short tons of aluminum for $14,836,000 to 11 companies, but dealers were surprised that Brown Industries won no metal.
Brown bid for about half the metal on offer at prices which normally would have secured a big chunk of metal, dealers said.
But in the award line-up announced late Thursday, Brown was absent.

The 11 successful bidders were Metal Exchange (1,000 tons), Global Minerals & Metals (750 tons), Alcoa (1,500 tons), Commercial Alloys (240 tons), J Pollock (240 tons), VAW America (740 tons), Mitsui (1,000 tons), Alumax (240 tons), Wise Metals (1,000), Tenneco Packaging 1,500 tons), and MG Metal Commodity Group (1,000 tons).
Industry sources said Brown Industries is operated by Floyd Brown, who was also of Aldridge Metals, a secondary metals company located in Chicago's south side.
Calls to Brown Industries were unreturned Friday morning.
Peter Roman, Stockpile's marketing manager, declined to comment on why Brown was not awarded metal, adding there are two criteria for winning metal in Stockpile sales.
"You have to bid high enough, and you have to be found responsive and responsible," Roman said
Responsive and responsible referred to a slew of issues such as being able to move the metal within 30 days, Roman added.
There was talk in the market prior to the award that Brown may have been late paying its $9 million bill after buying much of the zinc offered by Stockpile on May 20.

But other dealers believed Stockpile decided Thursday to exercise caution and not award another large amount of metal to a company without the profile or track record of a well-known trade house or producer.
Stockpile's Roman said of Brown: "They are not in default in zinc. They are in compliance with terms of the zinc contract as of today."
Any of last month's zinc buyers have 90 days from May 20 to pay for the zinc, Roman said.
